summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: @sxm-web/client-sdk-core@1.0.1 is a stub package whose only functional code is a beacon. The declared postinstall script runs `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is also invoked at require time from index.js. The beacon collects installer-side identifiers (hostname, install path, current working directory, Node.js version, package name) and POSTs them in cleartext over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc, which is unrelated to any legitimate registry or publisher infrastructure. The package's `main` returns a Proxy that produces no-op functions for every accessed property, so the package provides no advertised functionality — the install itself is the payload. The scoped name `@sxm-web/client-sdk-core` combined with a `Compatibility shim` description is consistent with a dependency-confusion probe aimed at an internal/private SDK namespace, where the beacon's purpose is to confirm successful resolution against private names and to disclose the resolving host's identity and filesystem layout to the operator at the bare IP.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
